title: Paul at Thessalonica, Berea, and Athens

questions.question: In Thessalonica, Paul reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue on how many Sabbaths?
options: Three Sabbaths
Seven Sabbaths
One Sabbath
Five Sabbaths
questions.explanation: Acts 17:2 (ESV): "And Paul went in, as was his custom, and on three Sabbath days he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,"

questions.question: Some were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas at Thessalonica. The Jews who were jealous gathered a mob and assaulted the house of which host?
options: Jason
Lydia
Timothy
Priscilla
questions.explanation: Acts 17:5-6 (ESV): "...the Jews were jealous... they formed a mob... they attacked the house of Jason..."

questions.question: The accusation about Paul and Silas in Thessalonica was that "These men who have turned the world upside down have come here also, and Jason has received them, and they are all acting against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king..."?
options: "Jesus."
"the Christ."
"the Lord."
"God alone."
questions.explanation: Acts 17:7 (ESV): "...saying that there is another king, Jesus."

questions.question: The Bereans were called "more noble" than the Thessalonians. Why?
options: They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so
They welcomed Paul with greater hospitality and generosity
Many more of them believed and they did not face opposition
They sent financial support for Paul's continued ministry
questions.correctAnswer: They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so
questions.explanation: Acts 17:11 (ESV): "Now these Jews were more noble than those in Thessalonica; they received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so."

questions.question: At Athens, Paul's spirit was provoked within him because the city was full of what?
options: Idols
Philosophers
Roman soldiers
Irreligious people
questions.explanation: Acts 17:16 (ESV): "Now while Paul was waiting for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw that the city was full of idols."

questions.question: Paul was brought to the Areopagus (Mars' Hill). The Epicurean and Stoic philosophers first called him a "babbler." What other title did they give him?
options: A preacher of foreign divinities
A foolish persuader of men
A Jewish agitator from the east
A wandering Sophist for hire
questions.explanation: Acts 17:18 (ESV): "Some said, 'What does this babbler wish to say?' Others said, 'He seems to be a preacher of foreign divinities'—because he was preaching Jesus and the resurrection."

questions.question: Paul noticed an altar with the inscription "To the unknown god." He used this as a starting point to proclaim what?
options: The God who made the world and everything in it, who is Lord of heaven and earth
Jesus as the fulfillment of all that the Greeks had been seeking
The resurrection as the final answer to all Greek philosophy
The one true God who alone deserves worship and sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The God who made the world and everything in it, who is Lord of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Acts 17:23-24 (ESV): "...'To the unknown god.' What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you. The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by man..."

questions.question: Paul said that God "made from one man every nation of mankind to live on all the face of the earth, having determined allotted periods and the boundaries of their dwelling place." What was God's goal in this?
options: That they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him
That they would know the true God through natural revelation
That his chosen people would be protected among the nations
That all nations would eventually send tribute to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: That they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him
questions.explanation: Acts 17:27 (ESV): "that they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him. Yet he is actually not far from each one of us,"

questions.question: Paul quoted a Greek poet saying "In him we live and move and have our being" and "For we are indeed his offspring." This was to argue that God cannot be what?
options: An image formed by art and the imagination of man
A concept created by human philosophy
A force limited to one nation or people
A deity who demands blood sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: An image formed by art and the imagination of man
questions.explanation: Acts 17:29 (ESV): "Being then God's offspring, we ought not to think that the divine being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by the art and imagination of man."

questions.question: Paul called all people to repent because God has "fixed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed; and of this he has given assurance to all by..."?
options: raising him from the dead
sending him as his Son
confirming him with signs
writing it in the Scriptures
questions.explanation: Acts 17:31 (ESV): "because he has fixed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed; and of this he has given assurance to all by raising him from the dead."

questions.question: When Paul mentioned the resurrection of the dead, how did the Athenians respond?
options: Some mocked, some wanted to hear more, and some believed
Most mocked and a significant minority believed
All mocked and no one in Athens believed
They debated the matter vigorously among themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Some mocked, some wanted to hear more, and some believed
questions.explanation: Acts 17:32-34 (ESV): "Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked. But others said, 'We will hear you again about this.' ...But some men joined him and believed..."

questions.question: Who were the named believers who joined Paul in Athens?
options: Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris
Gaius the host and Aristarchus the Macedonian
Jason and Secundus from Thessalonica
Sopater and Tychicus from Berea
questions.correctAnswer: Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris
questions.explanation: Acts 17:34 (ESV): "But some men joined him and believed, among whom also were Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris and others with them."

questions.question: The charge against Paul in Thessalonica was that he and his companions had "turned the world upside down." What was the official legal accusation before the city authorities?
options: Acting against the decrees of Caesar by saying there is another king, Jesus
Causing a riot and disturbing the civil peace of the city
Practising illegal religious rites forbidden by Roman law
Inciting the Jews to reject Roman taxation authority
questions.correctAnswer: Acting against the decrees of Caesar by saying there is another king, Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 17:7 (ESV): "and they are all acting against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."

questions.question: The crowd found Jason and dragged him before the city authorities. Jason was released after what was done?
options: He gave security (a bond) and was released
He swore an oath that Paul had already left the city
He paid a fine for hosting foreign agitators
He promised that Paul would not return to Thessalonica
questions.correctAnswer: He gave security (a bond) and was released
questions.explanation: Acts 17:9 (ESV): "And when they had taken money as security from Jason and the rest, they let them go."

questions.question: Paul said God "overlooked the times of ignorance, but now he commands all people everywhere to..."?
options: repent
believe
be saved
seek him
questions.explanation: Acts 17:30 (ESV): "The times of ignorance God overlooked, but now he commands all people everywhere to repent,"

key_verse_text: Now these Jews were more noble than those in Thessalonica; they received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so.
